text:
Predicates:
Barks(x) ::: x barks.
Dog(x) ::: x is a dog.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Jump(x) ::: x jumps.
HasLegs(x) ::: x has legs.
Terricolous(x) ::: x is terricolous.
KiKi ::: the animal named KiKi.

Premises:
¬Likes(Jane, x) if Barks(x) ::: Jane does not like animals that bark.
∀x (Dog(x) → Barks(x)) ::: All dogs are animals that bark.
∀x (Animal(x) → Jump(x)) if HasLegs(x) ::: Animals with legs jump.
∀x (Terricolous(x) → HasLegs(x)) ::: Terricolous animals have legs.
Animal(KiKi) ::: KiKi is an animal.
∀x ((¬Jump(x) ∧ ¬HasLegs(x)) → (Terricolous(x) ∨ HasLegs(x))) ::: If KiKi neither jumps nor has legs, then KiKi is terricolous or has legs.

Conclusion:
¬Barks(KiKi) ∧ ¬Dog(KiKi) ::: KiKi does not bark and is not a dog.
